content: If you experience any of the following symptoms, it may indicate a serious condition: persistent watery diarrhea, diarrhea that does not resolve, blood in your stool, severe stomach cramps, or a fever that begins after starting or stopping the medication. Additionally, rabeprazole can cause severe skin reactions, such as Stevens-Johnson Syndrome (SJS) or Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis (TEN), which can be life-threatening if untreated. If you develop a rash, stop taking rabeprazole immediately and contact your healthcare provider. Seek emergency medical attention if you notice symptoms of SJS or TEN, including painful red or purple skin that appears burned and peels, flat red rashes or blisters on the skin, mouth, nose, or genitals, red and painful watery eyes, or severe allergic reactions. Rabeprazole may also cause a specific allergic reaction known as DRESS (Drug Reaction with Eosinophilia and Systemic Symptoms), which can affect multiple organs, including the liver, kidneys, and heart. If you experience symptoms such as a skin rash, hives, fever, swollen lymph nodes, shortness of breath, swelling in the feet, ankles, or legs, dark-colored urine, or yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice), stop using the medication and seek medical help immediately. In some cases, rabeprazole can trigger or worsen lupus, an autoimmune disorder where the immune system attacks the body’s own tissues. Notify your healthcare provider if you develop new or worsening joint pain or a rash on your arms or cheeks. Long-term use of rabeprazole (three years or more) may lead to vitamin B-12 deficiency, as it reduces the absorption of this vitamin. Symptoms of deficiency include a sore tongue, weakness, or tingling and numbness in the hands or feet. Rabeprazole can also cause low magnesium levels (hypomagnesemia), which may result in seizures, heart rhythm problems, dizziness, muscle spasms, or changes in heart rate. Older adults and those taking the medication for extended periods or alongside other drugs that lower magnesium levels are at higher risk. If you experience any of these symptoms, stop taking rabeprazole and contact your healthcare provider. Rabeprazole may increase the risk of bone loss and fractures, particularly in older adults or those taking high doses or using the medication long-term. It can also cause severe allergic reactions, including breathing difficulties, a racing heart, swelling of the face, lips, or throat, trouble swallowing, itching, or hives. If you experience any of these symptoms, stop taking the medication and seek immediate medical attention. Rabeprazole should not be used by individuals allergic to its ingredients, other proton pump inhibitors, or specific components of the product. Consult your pharmacist for a complete list of ingredients. Additionally, rabeprazole may interact with other medications, such as methotrexate, digoxin, warfarin, tacrolimus, or certain antiretroviral drugs. Always inform your healthcare provider about all prescription and over-the-counter medications, vitamins, and supplements you are taking to avoid potential interactions. Do not take rabeprazole unless prescribed by a healthcare provider, and always follow the prescribed dosage. Do not share this medication with others, even if they have similar symptoms, as it may harm them. Keep rabeprazole out of reach of children, and do not chew, cut, or crush the tablets. While antacids may be taken alongside rabeprazole if needed, the medication is not intended for immediate relief of heartburn and may take 1 to 4 days to take full effect. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, consult your healthcare provider before using rabeprazole, as its effects on pregnancy and breast milk are not well understood. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember, unless it is close to the time for your next dose. In that case, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take double doses. In the event of an overdose, seek immediate medical attention by calling 911 or contacting a Poison Control Center at 800-222-1222.
